newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico outraged over light sentence for drug lord.
newsitem.headline: Mexico outraged over light sentence for drug lord.

text.p: The Mexican Attorney General's Office said on Tuesday it suffered a setback in the drug war when a judge handed a lenient sentence to an accused drug lord.

A judge in the western Mexican state of Jalisco sentenced Hector Palma Salazar to six years in prison on weapons charges but dismissed a host of other more serious drug trafficking allegations, the Attorney General's office said.
"Of course, this Attorney General's Office disagrees with the ruling of the judge," the top prosecuting body said in a news release.
Prosecutors said they would appeal the ruling and would continue to press other charges that could send Palma Salazar to prison for up to 33 years more.
The setback came one day after the Attorney General's Office announced the arrests of 25 members of the Juarez drug cartel, among them 16 police officers.
Authorities also confiscated three private jet planes, cash, cars and guns, but failed to arrest the leader of the cartel, Amado Carrillo Fuentes, also known as the "Lord of the Skies."
Carrillo Fuentes apparently escaped at the last minute when federal officers and Mexican soldiers raided his sister's wedding in the northwestern state of Sinaloa, the prosecutor's office reported.
Top law enforcment officials were claiming a major success in the arrests of Juarez cartel members. The cartel was reported to have shipped tons of cocaine through Mexican territory.
